subject: xxh128: speedup len [4,8]
perf_evidence: Subject 'xxh128: speedup len [4,8]': XXH3_len_4to8_128b replaces two independent 64-bit mixing chains (4 multiplies + 2 avalanches) by one 64x64->128 multiply plus cheap shifts.
change_summary: Pre-v0.8.0 output change of XXH3_len_4to8_128b (seed folded with swap32, single XXH_mult64to128(keyed, PRIME64_1), len added/subtracted to the halves, xor/shift cross-mix, avalanche both). Secondary hunk: new XXH_xorshift64 helper used in XXH3_avalanche, XXH3_len_4to8_64b and scalar XXH3_scrambleAcc (pure refactor).

notes: Intentional pre-v0.8.0 change of the XXH128 4..8-byte formula. Flags: -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize -w -DXXH_NO_INLINE_HINTS=1 -mllvm -inline-threshold=100000 -mllvm -inline-cold-callsite-threshold=100000 (the cold-callsite threshold is needed: XXH_likely/__builtin_expect branch weights make some call sites 'cold' (threshold 45) so e.g. XXH3_len_4to8_64b stayed out of line and both sides only compared calls to it -> fake 'correct'; xx_notes.json shows no residual calls in any target). Runner c/xxHash/_work2020/xx_alive.py, --smt-to 300000. Raw targets pass input (16 B) and secret (64 B) as noundef scalar args copied into fresh local buffers (no aliasing/poison). Api targets: input pointer + symbolic len bounded to the length class, seed symbolic; _withSecret targets take a secret pointer with secretSize>=136. 128-bit results are written through an out pointer; the api counterexample uses defined (non-poison) input bytes in a separate block, so it is not an aliasing/poison artefact; the raw counterexample (r_rawcex) uses only value args. Native sanity (native_x86_64/): over len 0..256 only XXH3_128bits for len 4..8 differs; XXH3_64bits/XXH32/XXH64 unchanged.
